entries.title: Comparison of Experiments
entries.author: David Blackwell
entries.bibliography: Proceedings of the Second Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability
entries.access_level: Primary PDF indexed summary and initial definitions retrieved; direct PDF access returned 403, so full-source rereading is not claimed
locators: Section 1: comparison by inclusion of all attainable risk profiles
Section 2: experiment as a collection of state-indexed probability measures
entries.adaptation: Restrict to deterministic signals and prove full-profile transport directly by composing a coarse policy with a fine-to-coarse decoding map.
entries.boundary: No new Blackwell theorem claimed. The arbitrary stochastic-experiment converse is not imported; the local binary-loss converse is proved independently for deterministic signal partitions.

entries.title: Equivalent Comparisons of Experiments
entries.author: David Blackwell
entries.access_level: Bibliographic record and author abstract checked through the collected-publications record; publisher full-text access blocked
entries.import: Classical equivalence between comparisons of statistical experiments is parent-owned.
entries.boundary: This attribution is not a claim to have reread or reproduced the complete 1953 proof. V7 supplies its own elementary deterministic proofs.

entries.title: Statistical Decision Functions
entries.author: Abraham Wald
entries.access_level: Indexed chapter headings and bibliographic record checked; full PDF retrieval unavailable
locators: 1.4.2: Decision Functions which Minimize the Maximum Risk (Minimax Solutions)
1.6: Interpretation of the Decision Problem as a Zero Sum Two-Person Game
entries.import: Maximum-risk decision criteria and their distinction from Bayes average-risk criteria are established statistical decision theory.
entries.boundary: No complete-class theorem, least-favorable-prior existence, minimax exchange theorem or statistical generalization result is imported.

entries.title: Prior-free Blackwell
entries.author: Maxwell Rosenthal
entries.access_level: Primary full PDF model, theorem, proof and timing sections read
locators: Section 3: known experiment, unknown state distribution, observed entire signal distribution
Section 3, page 4: pure versus mixed actions and adversary timing
Theorem 1: matrix factorization, null-space inclusion, identified-set inclusion and robust informativeness
Theorem 2 and Example 1: classical Blackwell order is stronger
entries.import: Probability-prior-free decision theory can retain substantial observation/objective assumptions; randomization and the adversary's timing affect value.
entries.boundary: Rosenthal observes an entire signal distribution; V7 observes a deterministic signal realization. His null-space criterion is not imported as V7's partition-refinement criterion or as a finite-sample guarantee.

entries.title: Recursive Multiple-Priors
entries.access_level: Author manuscript dated September 2002 read at rectangularity discussion and Theorem 3.2; publication is 2003
locators: Section 3.1: rectangularity relative to an information filtration
entries.import: Dynamic consistency under ambiguity has additional structural hypotheses and cannot be inferred from a one-step worst-case comparison.
entries.boundary: V7 does not implement recursive multiple-prior learning, Bayesian updates of a set of priors, or arbitrary robust sequential control.

claim_ownership.profile_transport: Parent information-order idea; direct composition proof and local kernel statement.
claim_ownership.binary_converse: Elementary separating-target argument for deterministic signals; no novelty claim.
claim_ownership.finite_minimax: Direct finite extrema and independent action-per-fiber proof; no interchange of unrestricted minimax operators.
claim_ownership.cost_crossover: Elementary scalar comparison under constant additive observation cost.
claim_ownership.randomization: Direct binary matching calculation; the agent's coin is not a probability prior over worlds.

evidence_contract: Primary-source access levels are explicit. Direct proofs determine local validity; citations do not turn missing source access, simulations, or finite tables into broader theorem authority.
